text: RSA 194 D sections three and four for annual meeting districts and Open Enrollment school must be established by a warrant article voted on by the school district. Because in last October, the New Hampshire Supreme Court ruled that unless a school district voted on how to manage open enrollment, the school district would be responsible for 80% of the costs of students going to another district. In addition, there is no cap on how many students could transfer into the school district. This means that without this proposed ward article, if a student chose to go to a school other than Claremont, the taxpayers would be responsible for paying 80% of the costs. This would reduce the amount of money available for our schools, and Claremont taxpayers would be paying to help fund a different town. For instance, if Claremont doesn't have this policy, it is roughly how the money would work if students wanted to transfer to another town. text: The attempted amendment failed. There are a few legal concerns with the petition language which I raised at the meeting. First, the governing law RSA 3215-F sets for the mandatory language, and that language requires that the budget cap be set as a dollar amount shown as blank dollars. Changing a dollar amount to a fiscal year reference is not permitted under the statute. Second, the language in the petition, because it does not follow the statute, also does not contain an actual figure that exists at the time of the meeting, or even a figure that is statutorily defined. While it is true that we are generally familiar with the term cost per pupil, and the New Hampshire Education Department calculates the cost per pupil for districts across the state, there is no single definition of cost per pupil in state law. For instance, RSA 189 colon 75 defines the cost per pupil, but that definition consists of three possible figures. As a result, on Election day, rather than asking voters to adopt a dollar cost per pupil, the voters will not know what number they are voting on because it is not clearly defined in the law and does not exist at the time of the vote.
